questions.q: Which principle of design deals with the distribution of visual weight within a composition?
questions.explain: Balance is the principle of design that relates to the distribution of visual weight in an artwork, ensuring that no single part of the composition overpowers another to the point of feeling unstable.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: When a composition is divided down the middle and both halves are exactly identical or mirror images of each other, what type of balance is achieved?
questions.explain: Symmetrical (or formal) balance occurs when the elements on one side of a design are identical, or nearly identical, to those on the other side of a central axis.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: An artwork features a single large, dark circle on the left side and three smaller, lighter circles on the right side, creating a feeling of stability despite being different. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Asymmetrical (informal) balance is achieved when the two sides of an artwork are not identical, but their visual weight is equalized. A large, heavy element can be balanced by multiple smaller, lighter elements.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: A decorative plate features a design where all the patterns and shapes start from the center point and fan out equally toward the circular edge. What kind of balance does this represent?
questions.explain: Radial balance is a form of balance where elements radiate outward from a common central point, similar to the spokes on a bicycle wheel or a circular mandala.
